BarChart.constructor.description: Create axes, grid lines, bars and optional category/value labels from the initial data. The established category order and vertical scale are reused by animateData.

parameters.options: Chart dimensions and theme, category/value data, optional yRange, colors and label formatting. Width and height use scene units.

notes: The constructor builds immediately. Calling build again appends another set of drawing entities; it does not clear the previous bars. Create a replacement chart deliberately when categories or domain change.

BarChart.animateIn.description: Prepare hidden, almost-zero-height bars, then return a staggered entrance animation. Preparation happens when this method is called; play the returned animation with Scene.play.

parameters.options: Duration in milliseconds; defaults to 1600. This entrance uses its own spring-like ease for each bar and a linear outer animation.

BarChart.animateIn.returnsDescription: An Animation to pass to Scene.play; this call does not start playback.
notes: The entrance restores the heights captured from the original data. Replaying it after animateData can therefore return to those original heights.

BarChart.animateData.description: Interpolate the heights of existing bars to new values on the existing vertical scale, preserving their baseline positions.

parameters.newData: Replacement values matched by array index. Keep the same category count and order; categories and colors are not rebuilt.
parameters.options: Duration defaults to 1200 milliseconds, and rate_func defaults to easeInOutCubic.

BarChart.animateData.returnsDescription: An Animation to play with Scene.play.
notes: It does not update options.data, category labels, the original entrance target heights or hover tooltip values. Store current application data separately.
Value labels switch to the target values while heights interpolate. Extra incoming entries are ignored; bars without an incoming entry retain their old geometry.

ValueTracker.animateValue.description: Build an animation toward an absolute numeric value. The tracker stores that number in Transform.t1 and draws no geometry.

parameters.targetValue: The final scalar in your application’s units. It replaces the current value rather than adding to it.

ValueTracker.animateValue.returnsDescription: An Animator builder. Pass it to Scene.play, supplying duration in milliseconds there.
notes: Read tracker.value in an updater to derive other geometry. Add the tracker to the scene alongside the objects using it.

Axes.c2p.description: Map mathematical x/y coordinates into the axes rectangle using its current ranges, width and height.

parameters.x: The horizontal mathematical coordinate. Values outside the range extrapolate.
parameters.y: The vertical mathematical coordinate. Values outside the range extrapolate.

Axes.c2p.returnsDescription: A new Vec3 with z = 0, centered around the axes rectangle’s origin.
notes: This calculation does not apply the axes entity or its parent transform. Despite the internal variable names, treat the returned point as coordinates of the untransformed axes rectangle; convert it explicitly when the axes are moved or rotated.

Axes.p2c.description: Convert a point in the axes rectangle’s untransformed coordinate space back to mathematical x/y values.

parameters.point: A Vec3 in the same coordinate space as Axes.c2p output. A world point must be transformed first if the axes are moved or rotated.

Axes.p2c.returnsDescription: An [x, y] tuple; access [0] and [1], not .x and .y.
notes: No clamping is applied. Clamp the result if interaction should remain within a chosen mathematical domain.

FunctionGraph2D.constructor.description: Sample a scalar function through a coordinate system and construct the selected line/fill primitives.

parameters.axes: The coordinate system defining the range and mathematical-to-scene mapping.
parameters.func: A synchronous scalar function y = f(x). Keep it finite and inexpensive over the sampled range.
parameters.options: Sampling/domain and paint settings. Defaults include cyan stroke, strokeWidth 0.08 and the coordinate system’s primitive, falling back to line3d.

notes: The constructor fills missing stroke fields on the supplied options object. Use a fresh options object if you need independent settings.

FunctionGraph2D.setFunction.description: Replace the sampled function and rebuild the curve immediately.

parameters.func: The new synchronous function y = f(x).

OrbitCameraController.constructor.description: Attach orbit, pan and zoom handling to a scene and camera. It initializes orbit direction from the current camera position and registers itself as scene.controls.

parameters.scene: The running scene whose canvas receives input. Construct the controller in Scene.run after the scene has started.
parameters.camera: The camera to control, usually scene.camera.
parameters.options: Optional targetCenter, radius, sensitivity, inertia and radius limits. Defaults include origin target, radius derived from current distance (or 20), and limits 0.1 to 5000.

notes: This constructor replaces scene.controls. Keep one controller per camera and dispose a controller explicitly when replacing it during a scene.
